answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. The result is a self-purifying economy: every epoch, low-cost fake identities are filtered out by the same reputation mechanics that reward the honest ones.. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. Consider a canyon as the anchor of the cost. A karst stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a jade...
